column1:
The FOMC statement is clearly constructive: repeated “strong” descriptors for activity and jobs, a rate hike to 2–2.25%, and “balanced” risks. The Beige Book corroborates this tone across Districts—reports from Dallas, Philadelphia, St. Louis, and Kansas City highlight ongoing job growth (notably in construction), Dallas notes firm consumer spending, and St. Louis describes solid manufacturing activity. Together, these real-economy reads support the Committee’s normalization path and align with SLOOS evidence of easier C&I standards and narrower loan-rate spreads. Netting these, the outlook is a bit stronger than initially assessed but still short of exuberant.
